query:
A group member commented on the Moorland Traverse plan in a way that combined a practical weather observation with a quiet expression of dissatisfaction about the outing format. Who made this comment?

Options:
A. Dmitri
B. Nadia
C. Marcus
D. Bridget
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t2 @2025-09-28T14:50:00) Moorland Traverse has a good weather window this time of year. Still a day hike though.
[2] (about=Nadia, episodic, t0 @2025-09-21T10:40:00) Thursday confirmed. Day hike though -- feels a bit short for that terrain.
[3] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2025-11-02T16:13:00) Cairn Ridge was the best outing. Overnight changes everything about how a route lands.
[4] (about=Marcus, episodic, t22 @2025-12-07T16:04:00) Good trip. Route held together, logistics were clean, no incidents. Nadia, that was an excellent piece of planning. The bothy capacity and the weather window aligned well.
[5] (about=Tomas, episodic, t2 @2025-09-28T14:43:00) The Moorland Traverse! Now we're talking. Past the limestone pavement near Haver's Edge there's a section where you can see three different geological periods in one exposed face. Back in the day that whole bit was just a farmers' track -- I've got photos from when they cut the path. Happy to plan the middle section if you want Marcus? Anyway who else got good shots today? 📸
[6] (about=Tomas, episodic, t12 @2025-11-02T16:08:00) Bracken Tor is a good recovery day -- there's a moraine field at the northern end that most people walk straight past without realising what they're looking at. I'll hold off on the geological tangent unless people want it. Back in the day that whole bowl was under ice. Anyway -- Bridget, genuinely well done on the overnight. Who else felt that was the group's best outing so far? 🗺️
[7] (about=Kwame, episodic, t12 @2025-11-02T16:19:00) ok real talk the campfire chat was one of my favourite group moments ever. Dmitri telling those field stories and Tomás doing the geology bit and everyone just being there in the dark up on the plateau. I wanted to record it so badly but I also just wanted to be in it, you know? 🔥
[8] (about=Elena, episodic, t2 @2025-09-28T14:54:00) There's a timed segment on the Moorland Traverse -- the pull up past the reservoir. Who's running it properly this time? 👀
[9] (about=Tomas, episodic, t18 @2025-11-23T16:02:00) The second col on the Stoneford continuation has a completely different geological character to the main summit -- you're on a different formation entirely past the saddle. Back in the day that whole section was marked on early OS maps as impassable in winter. Now it's just steep and interesting. Nadia this is a great call. Who else is in? 🗺️
[10] (about=Kwame, episodic, t4 @2025-10-05T15:50:00) Green Man YES 🙌🙌 also the traverse today was absolute scenes -- that section where the path just drops away and you can see like 40km in every direction?? I nearly cried ngl 😭✨ Tomás was giving us a full geology lecture which honestly I was here for
[11] (about=Bridget, core, t10 @2025-10-26T14:47:00) Confirmed for Cairn Ridge; asks about group tent pegs, cost-share for gas canisters, and weather contingency plan.
[12] (about=Bridget, core, t8 @2025-10-19T15:18:00) Prefers the western approach to Fenwick Edge as better managed and two kilometres shorter, based on old club experience.
[13] (about=GROUP, said_by=Bridget, group-interaction, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Bridget is driving from the east side for the bothy trip and can offer lifts from that direction.
[14] (about=Dmitri, core, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Confirmed for the bothy trip; believes the Stoneford continuation is terrain only doable properly with a night on it, wants more overnights.
[15] (about=Dmitri, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Gives step-by-step guidance on tricky terrain, encouraging trust in friction rather than fighting it.
[16] (about=Elena, core, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Confirmed for the bothy trip; mapped two timed segments on the approach, one on ascent to the col and one on ridge traverse.
[17] (about=Elena, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Wants to put a timed segment on the approach to the second col on the Stoneford continuation.
[18] (about=GROUP, said_by=Elena, group-interaction, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Two timed segments mapped on the bothy trip approach: one on ascent to the col, one on ridge traverse; times recorded at trailhead for anyone interested.
[19] (about=Kwame, said_by=Elena, profile, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Elena notes Kwame confused the reservoir ramp on the Moorland Traverse with the Ridgeback route, then corrected himself.
[20] (about=Kwame, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Volunteers to run the timed segment on the Moorland Traverse, saying he'll smash it this time.
[21] (about=Marcus, core, t10 @2025-10-26T14:47:00) Will handle the technical route for Cairn Ridge, including the north face approach.
[22] (about=Marcus, said_by=Saoirse, profile, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) Saoirse says the north face was solid, genuinely the kind of route that switches everything off.
[23] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Next week's hike is the Moorland Traverse, 610m gain, slightly more demanding; confirm participation by Thursday.
[24] (about=Nadia, said_by=self, core, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) Nadia says Cairn Ridge was the best outing; overnight changes everything about how a route lands.
[25] (about=Nadia, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Suggests doing Stoneford properly as an overnight using the bothy two kilometres past the summit that sleeps ten, noting the ridge continuation past the second col is only accessible if not rushing back.
[26] (about=Priya, core, t4 @2025-10-05T15:45:00) Took about 40 photos during the Moorland Traverse and is posting them; learned about the geological layers and wants to go back for that section.
[27] (about=Priya, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Excited about the bothy trip, asks if the route has steep sections.
[28] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Spring route plan should include at least one genuinely steep descent, not just moderately steep.
[29] (about=Saoirse, said_by=self, core, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) Saoirse says the north face was solid, genuinely the kind of route that switches everything off; could've done that section twice.
[30] (about=Saoirse, core, t0 @2025-09-21T10:00:00) Asks about terrain and technical difficulty before joining.
[31] (about=Tomas, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Offers to plan the middle section of the Moorland Traverse, mentioning limestone pavement near Haver's Edge with three geological periods and historical photos.
[32] (about=Tomas, core, t0 @2025-09-21T10:00:00) Prefers longer, more interesting route variants and shares historical/geological knowledge of the area.
[33] (about=GROUP, said_by=Tomas, group-interaction, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Spring plan includes a ridge system up north with a glacial cirque at the head, overnight only, that Tomas has wanted to do for years.
